newsitem.title: Belgium: TENNIS-BELGIUM COMPLETE 5-0 ROUT OF SPAIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BELGIUM COMPLETE 5-0 ROUT OF SPAIN.

text.p: Belgium trounced Spain 5-0 in the first round of the Fed Cup world group, inflicting two defeats on world number four Arantxa Sanchez Vicario in the process.
The former world number one, already beaten by substitute Els Callens on Saturday, lost again 6-3 2-6 8-6 to Belgium's leading player Sabine Appelmans in the reverse singles.

Callens later beat Spanish substitute Maria Luisa Serna 6-1 6-3 in the second reverse singles and teamed up with Nancy Feber to topple Gala Leon Garcia and Virginia Ruano-Pascual in the doubles 5-7 6-2 6-2.
Belgium will now face France in the semifinals.

Sanchez Vicario, who had won her six previous matches against world number 19 Appelmans, was under pressure from the start as she tried to protect Spain's fine record of winning the Cup four times in the past six years
She saved three set points in the ninth game of the first set but went down to the fourth when Appelmans hammered a double-fisted backhand down the line.
Appelmans tired in the second set but recovered her poise just in time, saving two break points in the first game of the final set.
She broke Sanchez in the sixth game and carved out a 5-2 lead. Sanchez Vicario broke back for 5-4 but finally went down amid thunderous applause from the partisan crowd.
"After the second set I thought I wouldn't make it. I was getting tired but then I found myself leading again," Appelmans said.
Spain were without Conchita Martinez, who formed with Sanchez Vicario the most successful doubles combination in Cup history. Martinez has tendinitis in her right shoulder.

Belgium were also weakened by the absence of Dominique Van Roost, who had not fully recovered from an abdomen injury which had forced her to retire in the quarter-finals of the Australian Open. Van Roost had knocked out Sanchez Vicario in the third round of the tournament.
